disease_state.evidence: De novo lipogenesis (DNL) has been implicated in the development and progression of hepatic liver steatosis.

Both semi-purified diets resulted in increased body weight, fat mass and liver triglyceride content compared to chow-fed mice while hepatic DNL was increased in the high starch fed mice and decreased in the high fat fed mice.

material_type.evidence: Proteomic analysis was carried out on the livers of these mice and proteins were identified that associated with either the rate of DNL or triglyceride content in the liver.

sample_source.evidence: Proteomic analysis was carried out on the livers of these mice and proteins were identified that associated with either the rate of DNL or triglyceride content in the liver.

sex.evidence: Male C57BL/6J mice were fed either a standard chow diet a semi-purified high starch diet or a high fat diet.

strain.evidence: Male C57BL/6J mice were fed either a standard chow diet a semi-purified high starch diet or a high fat diet.
